claims.text: POL-RD-24(a) is the only row that leaves a deviating driver with the whole of the trip's charge, and it requires that the rider have been 'informed and agreed'. The driver's notice limb under POL-RD-21 does appear satisfied - his chat at 19:34:22 preceded the exit at the KPE / Sims Way exit - but notice is not agreement, and POL-RD-21 makes a deviation 'agreed' only where the chat log or a call recording confirms the rider's acknowledgment. This chat log records the opposite: the driver asked 'I come out at Sims Ave and go Aljunied ok?' (MSG-05008-003) and the rider refused in terms, 'No need, pls just stay on KPE, I don't mind the jam' (MSG-05008-004), repeating the objection after the exit, 'Eh I said no need already, why still exit' (MSG-05008-005). There is no acknowledgment, so row (a) is unavailable and the driver cannot make the no-refund case he filed.

The deviation is on the record and over tolerance, and the matrix's own measure of it is 1.08 SGD. POL-RD-22 takes the platform's recorded distances - actual 11.4 km against recommended 9.9 km - giving a deviation of 1.50 km against the 1.0 km tolerance, so the within-tolerance rows cannot apply and the only refund the matrix supplies for a non-agreed deviation over tolerance is the excess distance fare: 1.50 km x 0.72 SGD per km = 1.08 SGD, without surge, rounded to the cent (POL-RD-24, excess_distance_fare formula). That figure is exactly the amount contested in this dispute.

The 1.08 SGD the driver sues for is not a windfall held by the rider; it is precisely the excess distance fare POL-RD-24 measures, and the payments ledger and trip record show it already refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver (refund_issued_sgd 1.08; payment_status PARTIALLY_REFUNDED; fare_adjusted at 2026-08-21T20:48:23). The driver asks for that sum back, but no row of POL-RD-24 produces DRIVER_COMPENSATION - the clause licenses only NO_ACTION, PARTIAL_REFUND and ESCALATE - and under POL-GEN-03 NO_ACTION preserves the present state and never means 'restore a charge'. The driver's claim is therefore unsupported and the present state, with the 1.08 SGD with the rider, stands.

If the judge takes the facts as they stand - a driver who notified the rider by chat and a rider who objected - the case is the very example POL-RD-24 reserves: a case that fits no row (for example, informed but the rider objected) is escalated under POL-GEN-26. Escalation issues no monetary outcome and holds the amount (POL-GEN-03), so on that path too the 1.08 SGD stays with the rider rather than being collected back from her by the driver. The rider's position is protected on either reading.

The LTA advisory does not carry the driver's claim. Its type (HEAVY_TRAFFIC) is within POL-RD-23's congestion vocabulary and its window 19:09-20:19 overlaps the trip, but the evidence package leaves its intersection with the recommended route to the judge - the derived intersects_route and justifies_reroute are both null and the package states the record does not say whether the advisory lies on the recommended route. Either way, traffic justification feeds only rows (a) and (b) of POL-RD-24: row (b) still requires the excess distance fare to be refunded to the rider, and row (a) is barred by the rider's refusal. Justification cannot convert this dispute into a payment to the driver.

claims.text: The driver gave the rider in-app notice before leaving the recommended route, which is all POL-RD-21 asks for. MSG-05008-003 was sent at 2026-08-21T19:34:22, delivered at 19:34:23 and read by the rider at 19:35:00, and it stated a brief reason: 'KPE very jam after Sims Way, I come out at Sims Ave and go Aljunied ok? Faster.' The platform's own route_deviation_detected event is timestamped 19:37:02, and the trace does not place the vehicle off KPE until the 19:36:53 fix on Sims Avenue, so the notice precedes the deviation on either timestamp. The notice limb of POL-RD-21 is therefore satisfied on the record, and every refund argument built on 'the rider was not informed' is excluded.

The reroute was traffic-justified under POL-RD-23. EV-ADVIS-05008-01 is an LTA advisory of type HEAVY_TRAFFIC, which falls in the congestion class POL-RD-23 admits; its road field is 'Kallang-Paya Lebar Expressway (KPE)', the same named road the recommended route uses (optimal_route_via includes KPE), its direction is 'towards TPE' and its location_desc is 'after Sims Way exit', which is the very point the trip record identifies as the deviation point ('Vehicle left the recommended route at KPE / Sims Way exit'). It is valid from 19:09:23 to 20:19:23 and overlaps the trip window (19:29:23 to 19:52:23), so the congestion is documented for the recommended-route segment at the trip time and the driver's reason for exiting was not mere assertion.

The detour was confined to the congested stretch and the driver returned to the recommended route: the trace shows the vehicle on the KPE until the 19:36:23 fix, on Sims Avenue from 19:36:53, and the trip record logs route_rejoined at 19:50:37 at Upper Serangoon Road / Hougang Avenue 1, a road the recommended route itself uses before the drop-off. That is a discrete real-time response to congestion of the kind POL-RD-21 permits, not a gratuitous route change, and it gave the rider a shorter, moving route rather than a stationary one.

Neither refund row in POL-RD-24 is available on this record, because each one requires a fact the evidence contradicts. Row (b) requires that the rider was not informed, but MSG-05008-003 was delivered at 19:34:23 and read at 19:35:00, two minutes before the deviation; row (d) requires that the reroute was not traffic-justified, and EV-ADVIS-05008-01 documents heavy congestion on the KPE towards TPE after Sims Way exit inside the trip window. The 1.08 SGD recovered from the driver's earnings at 20:48:23 therefore rests on no row of POL-RD-24.

The deviation is measured under POL-RD-22 on the platform's recorded distances: 11.4 km actual minus 9.9 km recommended is 1.50 km, above the 1.0 km tolerance the clause sets (the sparse trace is not used to re-measure the distance). Rows (c) and (e) are therefore unavailable, and the case turns solely on the notice and traffic-justification limbs, both of which the record answers in the driver's favour.

The present state moves 1.08 SGD of the driver's earnings for conduct that no row of POL-RD-24 makes refundable. POL-GEN-03 gives the ruling value for that: the driver is owed the money back, so DRIVER_COMPENSATION with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both 1.08. Because the contested amount is 1.08 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, an AI ruling is final at any confidence; driver_profile.fraud_flags is 0, so no elevated confidence threshold applies, and POL-RD-25's 2 km limb is not applied (ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied is false) and in any event the 1.50 km deviation is within it.

Even on the reading that the rider's message 'No need, pls just stay on KPE, I don't mind the jam' takes this case outside every row of POL-RD-24, the consequence POL-RD-24 itself names for a case that fits no row is escalation under POL-GEN-26 - the amount is held for the human reviewer. A rider objection is nowhere made a ground of refund by POL-RD-24, so on no reading of the matrix does the 1.08 SGD simply stay with the rider; the most the rider's objection can do is send the money to a human, not award it to her.

ruling.explanation:
Each side is partly right, but the rule that decides this case sends it to a human reviewer rather than to either party's pocket.

WHAT THE RECORD SHOWS. The driver left the recommended route at the KPE / Sims Way exit at 19:37:02 and rejoined at Upper Serangoon Road / Hougang Avenue 1 at 19:50:37. Under POL-RD-22 the deviation is measured on the platform's recorded distances, 11.4 km actual against 9.9 km recommended = 1.50 km, which is over the 1.0 km tolerance. The excess distance fare is 1.50 km x 0.72 SGD per km = 1.08 SGD (POL-RD-24, excess_distance_fare formula, no surge) - exactly the sum refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver's earnings at 20:48:23 (refund_issued_sgd 1.08; total trip charge 22.11 SGD).

NOTICE AND AGREEMENT (POL-RD-21). The driver's chat at 19:34:22, 'Miss, KPE very jam after Sims Way, I come out at Sims Ave and go Aljunied ok? Faster', preceded the exit on any timestamp, so the notice limb is met - the driver is right on that, and the finding stands. But the rider answered at 19:34:52, 'No need, pls just stay on KPE, I don't mind the jam', and repeated the objection at 19:38:22. POL-RD-21 makes a deviation 'agreed' only where the chat log or a call recording confirms the rider's acknowledgment. There is no acknowledgment here. The deviation is therefore informed but not agreed.

TRAFFIC JUSTIFICATION (POL-RD-23). The LTA record (EV-ADVIS-05008-01) is a HEAVY_TRAFFIC advisory on the Kallang-Paya Lebar Expressway (towards TPE) after the Sims Way exit, valid 19:09:23 to 20:19:23 and so overlapping the trip window (19:29:23 to 19:52:23). That road is the recommended route's own road, the direction is the route's direction of travel, and the location is the recommended route immediately beyond the point the trip record itself marks as the deviation - the same jam the driver cited at the time. The package left this intersection to the judge because the derived intersects_route and justifies_reroute fields are null; deciding it on road, direction and location as POL-RD-23 directs, I find the advisory intersects the recommended route and the reroute was traffic-justified.

THE MATRIX (POL-RD-24) - NO ROW APPLIES. Row (a) needs the rider to have agreed; she did not. Row (b) needs the rider not to have been informed; she was. Rows (c) and (e) need a deviation of 1 km or less; it is 1.50 km. Row (d) needs the reroute not to be traffic-justified; it was. POL-RD-24 says that a case fitting no row - its own example being 'informed but the rider objected' - is escalated under POL-GEN-26. That is this case.

OUTCOME. ESCALATE is terminal (POL-GEN-03): no money issues to either side, and the 1.08 SGD is held by the platform - not paid back to the driver and not released to the rider - pending a human reviewer.

THE DRIVER'S CLAIMS. The findings on notice, on traffic justification and on the 1.50 km deviation are accepted, as is the point that the excess distance fare measures 1.08 SGD. They do not produce the payment the driver asks for. The 1.08 SGD cannot come back to the driver: no row of POL-RD-24 licenses DRIVER_COMPENSATION, and POL-GEN-03's NO_ACTION would only preserve the present state, never restore a charge - and in any event this case fits no no-refund row. The driver's alternative claim is accepted: the most the rider's objection can do is send the money to a human reviewer, and that is what happens here.

THE RIDER'S CLAIMS. Her arithmetic and ledger facts (1.50 km x 0.72 = 1.08 SGD; refund_issued_sgd 1.08; PARTIALLY_REFUNDED) are accepted, and she is right that row (a) is unavailable for want of her agreement. But the rows that would pay that 1.08 SGD to her each fail on their own condition - row (b) because she was informed, row (d) because the reroute was traffic-justified - so the money does not simply stay with her either; POL-RD-24 escalates it. Her reading of the LTA package as leaving the route intersection to the judge is correct and is answered above; that finding removes row (d) but converts nothing into a payment to the driver, which is her central point and it is upheld.

EVIDENCE WEIGHT. The trip record, GPS trace, chat log, fare breakdown and LTA advisory all carry weight 1.0 and are complete, so nothing under POL-GEN-02 lowers confidence; the confidence stated is above the 0.80 POL-RD-25 requires. No clause in this category produces a referral on a route deviation, so the referrals list is empty.

OPEN QUESTIONS FOR THE HUMAN REVIEWER (not referrals): whether a driver who proceeds after an express refusal should still keep the excess distance fare, and whether the interim 1.08 SGD adjustment should be finalised or reversed.

ruling.explanation:
Mr Driver and Ms Rider, I have read the platform trip record, the driver's GPS trace, the in-app chat log, the fare ledger and the LTA traffic advisory, and applied the route-deviation policy.

WHAT IS ESTABLISHED. The trip from Suntec City to Heartland Mall Kovan was recorded at 11.4 km against a recommended 9.9 km, a deviation of 1.50 km, above the 1.0 km tolerance (POL-RD-22; EV-TRIP-05008). The reroute was traffic-justified: the LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-05008-01 reports heavy traffic on the KPE towards TPE after Sims Way exit, valid 19:09-20:19 and so overlapping the trip window of 19:29-19:52, on the road and in the direction the recommended route itself uses (POL-RD-23). Mr Driver, you did give notice: your chat MSG-05008-003 was sent at 19:34:22 and read at 19:35:00, before the vehicle left the recommended route at 19:37:02 (POL-RD-21; EV-CHAT-05008, EV-TRIP-05008). But Ms Rider did not agree. POL-RD-21 makes a deviation 'agreed' only where the chat log or a call recording confirms the rider's acknowledgment, and the chat records the opposite: you asked 'I come out at Sims Ave and go Aljunied ok?' and she replied at 19:34:52 'No need, pls just stay on KPE, I don't mind the jam', repeating the objection at 19:38:22, 'Eh I said no need already, why still exit'. The exit went ahead against that refusal.

WHY THIS GOES TO A HUMAN. POL-RD-24 supplies five rows and exactly one must apply. Row (a) needs the rider informed AND agreed: she was informed but did not agree. Row (b) needs the rider NOT informed: she was informed. Rows (c) and (e) need a deviation of 1 km or less: it was 1.50 km. Row (d) needs the reroute NOT traffic-justified: it was justified. No row fits, and POL-RD-24 says in terms that a case which fits no row - its own example is 'informed but the rider objected' - is escalated under POL-GEN-26. This case is that example, so I escalate it (POL-RD-24, POL-GEN-26).

WHAT THAT MEANS FOR THE 1.08 SGD. ESCALATE is terminal and replaces any money outcome (POL-GEN-03): no amount is collected and none is refunded on my ruling, and the 1.08 SGD refunded to Ms Rider and recovered from Mr Driver on 21 Aug 2026 at 20:48 (EV-FARE-05008, EV-TRIP-05008) is held for the human reviewer. Notice (POL-RD-21). The driver's chat at 19:34:22 — 'KPE very jam after Sims Way, I come out at Sims Ave and go Aljunied ok? Faster.' — was delivered 19:34:23 and read 19:35:00 (EV-CHAT-05008), before the platform's 19:37:02 route_deviation_detected event and before the trace places the car off the KPE. The notice limb is met, so the argument that the rider was not informed fails.

Agreement (POL-RD-21). A deviation is 'agreed' only where the chat log or a call recording confirms the rider's acknowledgment. The chat log records the opposite: at 19:34:52 the rider wrote 'No need, pls just stay on KPE, I don't mind the jam', and repeated it at 19:38:22 after the exit. Row (a) of POL-RD-24 (traffic-justified, informed and agreed: no refund) therefore cannot apply, and the driver cannot make the no-refund case he filed.

Traffic justification (POL-RD-23). EV-ADVIS-05008-01 is an LTA HEAVY_TRAFFIC advisory for the KPE (towards TPE) after Sims Way exit — the road the recommended route uses and the very point the trip record identifies as the deviation point — valid 19:09:23 to 20:19:23, overlapping the trip window (19:29:23 to 19:52:23). Read against the trip, it intersects the recommended route, so the reroute was traffic-justified and row (d) (not traffic-justified: refund) does not apply either. The driver's rejoin at Upper Serangoon Road / Hougang Avenue 1 (19:50:37) confirms the detour was confined to that stretch, but it does not change the row analysis.

The driver's request for DRIVER_COMPENSATION of 1.08 SGD is not available: POL-RD-24 licenses only NO_ACTION, PARTIAL_REFUND and ESCALATE, and no row of the matrix produces POL-GEN-03's DRIVER_COMPENSATION. Nor is the present state simply confirmed as standing; escalation holds the money rather than awarding it to either party.

No referral clause applies to a route deviation in this version, so none is issued.

Open question for the human reviewer (in explanation only, not a referral): how to treat a rider's express refusal of a reroute that the driver notified and that traffic justified — whether the 1.08 SGD excess distance fare stays with the rider, returns to the driver, or is split; the refund matrix does not say.
